slot.brief: For a cubic, find the point of inflexion by setting f''(x) = 0 and check sign change.

stem: A cubic curve has stationary points at $(1,9)$ and $(3,5)$. Its point of inflexion is:

verdicts.working: The inflection point’s x-coordinate is the midpoint of the stationary points: x=2. For a cubic, values at points equally spaced around its inflection point average to the value there, so y=(9+5)/2=7.

working:
$f'(x)=k(x-1)(x-3)$.
$f(3)-f(1)=k\displaystyle\int_1^3(x-1)(x-3)\,dx=-\dfrac{4k}{3}=-4\Rightarrow k=3$.
$f''(x)=6(x-2)$, which changes sign at $x=2$.
$f(2)=f(1)+\displaystyle\int_1^2 3(x-1)(x-3)\,dx=9-2=7$.
Point of inflexion: $(2,7)$.
